conditions.overall: Small headwater streams in WNC are the top option this time of year, running cool and well-oxygenated. The Watauga has returned to normal summer flows after 3 weeks of high water, while the South Holston has been running low for several weeks.

tactics: Use a dry dropper setup on small headwater streams — keep flies small and light, and be stealthy. Throwing a huge dry fly will spook fish just like throwing an indicator would.
After rain events when water is up and dingy on wild streams, switch to small Pat's Rubber Legs (#12-14) and squirmy worms, with a larger Chernobyl (#12) to float the heavier flies.

On the Watauga, fish the cold morning pulse (typically 6–7 AM) with light dry dropper setups — generation starts at 1 PM Mon–Fri and noon on Saturday, with no generation on Sunday except the morning pulse.
On the South Holston, fish during the three short hourly pulses each day and lengthen your leader with light tippet (6x–6.5x) — fish can be spooky under low water conditions.
Use the North Carolina Interactive Trout Map to find new wild trout streams in the area.
Always check current TVA dam release schedules before heading out to the Watauga or South Holston — flows can change without notice.

waters.name: WNC Small Headwater Streams
waters.note: It's small stream season. These streams stay cooler and have a lot of elevation change that keeps water well oxygenated. Best production is on these streams right now. Use dry dropper setups with small, light flies.

waters.name: Watauga River
waters.note: After 3 straight weeks of high water, the Watauga has returned to normal summer flows — low water in the morning with an hour-long pulse from 6–7 AM, and high water in the afternoon. Generation starts at 1 PM Mon–Fri and noon Saturday; no generation Sunday except the morning pulse. Fishing has been excellent — light dry dropper setups have been very successful most days, and sporadic sulphur hatches are still occurring in the morning.

waters.name: South Holston River
waters.note: Flows have been low for several weeks with 3 short hourly pulses each day — great for wade fishing. Fish a light dry dropper setup, lengthen your leader, and use light tippet (6x–6.5x) as fish can be spooky in low water.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone, 3300-4000ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC
